newsitem.title: USA: NYC alters Coney Island hospital deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC alters Coney Island hospital deal - paper.

text.p: New York City's Giuliani Administration quietly changed the deal to lease Coney Island Hospital to a private company for 99 years, allowing it to take ownership after seven years, Newsday said Friday.

David Jones, a member of the city Health and Hospitals Corp board, who opposed the deal, made the revised contract public on Thursday, charging that a major change had been made after its approval, the paper said.
The sale was ruled illegal in a court order Mayor Rudolph Giuliani is appealing. In the meantime, city officials have been moving to finalize the details and sign contracts.
City officials previously have said the long-term lease would let New York City assure that the private company, Primary Health Systems, keep its commitment to provide quality care, Newsday said.

A spokeswoman for the Health and Hospitals Corp minimized the change, saying any sale would have to be approved by the City Council, the paper added. The Council is against the deal, and it filed the lawsuit that halted it.
